title: The Phoenician circumnavigation of Africa, c. 600 BC
summary: Pharaoh Necho II sends Phoenician sailors down the Red Sea, with orders to return by the Pillars of Heracles; each autumn they land and sow a crop, and in the third year they come home to Egypt. Herodotus doubts the sun on their right hand. The course is the story told, drawn with a broad brush.

events.label: The Phoenicians put out from the Red Sea
events.text: Herodotus says that Pharaoh Necho sent Phoenicians down the Red Sea and told them to come home through the Pillars of Heracles, the Strait of Gibraltar. Each autumn they landed, sowed grain, waited for the harvest, and put out again.

events.label: Round Libya (Africa): the sun on the right hand
events.text: Herodotus doesn't believe it: the crews claimed that, in rounding Libya, they had the sun on their right hand. That odd detail, the sun in the north, is just what sailors in the southern hemisphere would see, and what makes the story likely to be true.
